FAQ

Connection and installation issues

Connection refused (Connection refused)

Phenomenon: When calling any interface, ConnectionError or Connection refused is reported.

Cause: The atom_vp_interface service is not running, or the base_url configuration is incorrect.

Solution steps:

  1. Verify that the service is running:

    curl http://127.0.0.1:10026/Graph/GetAllGraphsNoThumbnail

  2. If the service is on another port, modify base_url:

    client = AtomClient(base_url="http://127.0.0.1:your port number")

  3. If the service is on another machine, replace IP:

    client = AtomClient(base_url="http://192.168.1.100:10026")

Python package cannot be found

Phenomenon: The installation command cannot find atom_sdk or the wheel file.

Solution: Download and extract the SDK archive from the Download Center, then install the local wheel:

python -m pip install <SDK_DIR>/python/atom_sdk-<version>-*.whl

Confirm that the wheel matches your Python version and operating system. Activate your virtual environment first if you use one.

Timestamp related

The data has been modified and needs to be synchronized. Please obtain the graph again.

Phenomenon: An error occurs when calling editing interfaces such as create_node and set_node_param_data. The error message includes "data has been modified" or "synchronization is required".

Cause: The graph version you hold (timestamp) has expired. Another operation (perhaps a front-end edit, another script, or one of your previous operations) modified the diagram, causing a version mismatch.

Solution steps:

  1. Main image operation: Recall open_graph() Refresh timestamp

    client.graph.open_graph("my_graph")
# Then retry your operation

  2. Subgraph operation: Recall graph_node.open_graph()

    from atom_sdk import SubGraphRef

client.graph_node.open_graph(SubGraphRef("my_graph", graph_node_id))

Common trigger scenarios:

  • Modify the same picture in the Atom front-end interface and script at the same time

  • Multiple scripts modify the same picture concurrently

  • The script waits for a long time after opening the graph before continuing.

Do I need to pass timestamp for every operation?

unnecessary. SDK automatically caches timestamp after successful operations such as open_graph(), create_node(), etc., and will be automatically carried by subsequent operations without manual transmission.

Service and interface selection

What is the difference between NodeService and GraphNodeService?

  • NodeService (client.node): operate nodes in main graph

  • GraphNodeService (client.graph_node): Operate nodes inside subgraph nodes

The subgraph node is a special node in the main graph, which contains a complete subgraph. All methods of GraphNodeService have one more parameter than NodeService graph_node_id, which is used to specify which subgraph to enter.

If you are not sure which one to use, first use open_graph to get the node list and determine the node type.

The difference between graph_node_id and node_id

In GraphNodeService, methods usually have two ID parameters:

  • graph_node_id: ID of the subgraph node itself in the main graph (the one created with client.node.create_node)

  • node_id: ID of a node inside the subgraph (the one created with client.graph_node.create_node)

Passing an error may not necessarily report an error, but it will operate on the wrong node.

Parameter setting problem

There is no change in the running results after setting the parameters.

Possible reasons:

  1. param_type typo: init_params and run_params are different. Check the node definition to confirm:

    from atom_sdk import NodeRef

info = client.node.get_node_info_in_graph(NodeRef("my_graph", node_id))
print([p["name"] for p in info["nodeInfo"].get("initParams", [])])
print([p["name"] for p in info["nodeInfo"].get("runParams", [])])

  2. init_params is set but not initial_node: Re-initialization is required after modifying init_params:

    from atom_sdk import NodeRef

client.node.initial_node(NodeRef("my_graph", node_id))

  3. param_name case error: The parameter name is case-sensitive, and the name returned by get_node_info_in_graph shall prevail.

How to upload file parameters

# Python:pass pathlib.Path object,SDK Automatic upload
from pathlib import Path
from atom_sdk import NodeParamUpdate

client.node.set_node_param_data(
    NodeParamUpdate(
        "my_graph", node_id,
        "model", "init_params",
        Path("/absolute/path/to/model.bin")  # Path object
    )
)

Passing a string path will not trigger file upload and will be written as an ordinary string parameter.

RuntimeFrame related

RuntimeService.run_graph Let’s look at the input mode first: the normal mode uses RuntimeFrame that encapsulates the complete EPICRAW, and the passive binocular passive_bino mode uses RuntimePassiveBinoFrame.

run_graph reports that frame is missing EPICRAW

Phenomena: ValueError: runtime frame is missing EPICRAW bytes

Cause: Every RuntimeFrame in normal mode must contain a non-empty copy of EPICRAW.

correct format:

from atom_sdk import RuntimeFrame, RuntimeRunParams

frame = RuntimeFrame.from_file("frame.epicraw", cam2_base=[x, y, z, rx, ry, rz], roi=None)
result = client.runtime.run_graph(RuntimeRunParams("my_graph", [frame]))
print("Run request status:", result["status"])

If EpicProInput in the picture is configured as passive_bino, do not fill in image or point_cloud in this format. Python please use RuntimeRunParams.passive_bino_from_file(…​) or passive_bino_from_images(…​); C++ please use RuntimeRunParams::passive_bino_from_file/bytes/images(…​); C# please use RuntimeRunParams.PassiveBinoFromFile/Bytes/Images(…​).

What format should image and point_cloud be sent?

  • image: Raw uncompressed pixel bytes, not JPEG/PNG. Convert with numpy_array.tobytes():

    import numpy as np
image_bytes = np.zeros((480, 640, 3), dtype=np.uint8).tobytes()

  • point_cloud: float32 raw bytes, shape is [H, W, 3]:

    pc_bytes = np.zeros((480, 640, 3), dtype=np.float32).tobytes()

Points type point cloud related

run_single_node_no_graph buffer size must be a multiple of element size

Phenomena: AtomApiError: buffer size must be a multiple of element size

Reason: The input port of type Points/XYZPoints/NormalPoints/RGBPoints requires the input of binary data in the server’s custom protocol format ([点云个数, 每份长度, 数据…​]), which is not an ordinary file. The new version SDK will automatically encode the .ply path into this binary according to the node input port type; if you are using the old version SDK, SDK and cannot find the node input type, or you have passed the original xyz bytes that lack the protocol header, the server may report this error when parsing according to float32.

Solution steps:

  1. Prioritize directly passing the .ply path and let SDK automatically handle it according to the node port type.

  2. If the node type cannot be queried automatically, explicitly supplement input_data_types={"points": "XYZPoints"} to SingleNodeParams.

  3. If you want to manually control the point dimensions, you can use load_ply_points + encode_point_cloud_payload to generate the bytes required by the protocol.

Directly pass the .ply path:

from atom_sdk import SingleNodeParams

result = client.runtime.run_single_node_no_graph(
    SingleNodeParams("EstimateNormal", inputs={"points": "/data/scan.ply"})
)

Manual coding:

from atom_sdk import SingleNodeParams, encode_point_cloud_payload, load_ply_points

points = load_ply_points("/data/scan.ply")
payload = encode_point_cloud_payload(points, point_dim=3)

result = client.runtime.run_single_node_no_graph(
    SingleNodeParams("EstimateNormal", inputs={"points": payload})
)

Common trigger scenarios:

  • Directly write inputs={"points": "/data/scan.ply"} in the old SDK

  • The node type cannot be automatically queried, and there is no manual filling input_data_types

  • I spelled out the original float32 bytes of xyz myself, but missed the [点云个数, 长度] header information required by the protocol.

See Binary protocol for point cloud type input and output for detailed protocol format.

run_single_node_no_graph returns bytes, not the expected dict

Phenomenon: After calling run_single_node_no_graph, type(result) is bytes, and doing result["xxx"] on it will report TypeError: byte indices must be integers.

Reason: For CalculateEdge, CalculateEdgeNew, EstimateNormal, DownSample, DownSampleWithNormal, FilterByNormal, the server directly returns the unencapsulated original point cloud bytes (content-type: application/octet-stream, but not the "JSON header + named attachment" format in the SDK conventional binary protocol). SDK Attempts to decode using conventional methods will fail, so the design falls back to returning directly to the original bytes.

Solution steps:

  1. Before calling, confirm whether the node name is in the special list above. The expected result is bytes.

  2. Use decode_point_cloud_payload to parse, has_dim_in_header fixedly passes False, point_dim is selected according to the actual type of the node output port (XYZPoints/Points passes 3, NormalPoints/RGBPoints passes 6):

    from atom_sdk import decode_point_cloud_payload

result = client.runtime.run_single_node_no_graph(
    SingleNodeParams("EstimateNormal", inputs={"points": payload})
)
clouds = decode_point_cloud_payload(result, has_dim_in_header=False, point_dim=6)
print(clouds[0].shape)          # (Points, 6) -> [x, y, z, nx, ny, nz]

Common trigger scenarios:

  • Call run_single_node_no_graph as a normal node and directly obtain the dictionary field from the return value

  • point_dim is transmitted incorrectly, resulting in data misalignment after reshape

C++ related

C++ How to read atom::sdk::JsonValue return value

auto result = client.graph().create_graph({"my_graph"});
std::cout << "Request status:" << result.at("status").get<std::int64_t>() << std::endl;

// Read string
std::string graph_id = result.at("graphId").get<std::string>();

// read numbers
double ts = result.at("timestamp").get<double>();

// Determine whether the field exists
if (result.contains("optional_field")) {
    // ...
}

set_node_param_data How to select value type

C++ Use NodeParamUpdate to pass in complete parameters, value can be a JSON value or a file path:

// pass JSON value(threshold,configuration etc.)
client.node().set_node_param_data(
    {"my_graph", node_id, "threshold", "run_params",
     atom::sdk::JsonValue(0.7)}
);

// Pass file path(Model files, etc.,Automatic upload)
client.node().set_node_param_data(
    {"my_graph", node_id, "model", "init_params",
     std::filesystem::path("/path/to/model.bin")}
);

C# related

C# SDK Is there any synchronization method?

C# SDK are all async methods. In scenarios where async is not supported (such as console synchronization code), you can:

// way1:.GetAwaiter().GetResult()(Block the current thread)
var result = client.Graph.CreateGraphAsync(new CreateGraphParams("my_graph")).GetAwaiter().GetResult();

// way2:Task.Run(Run in thread pool)
var result = Task.Run(() => client.Graph.CreateGraphAsync(new CreateGraphParams("my_graph"))).Result;

In ASP.NET or other asynchronous frameworks, always use await, do not use the above synchronous writing (may cause deadlock).

C# JsonElement How to read fields

var result = await client.Graph.CreateGraphAsync(new CreateGraphParams("my_graph"));

// Read string
string graphId = result.GetProperty("graphId").GetString()!;

// read numbers
double timestamp = result.GetProperty("timestamp").GetDouble();

// Read request status
int status = result.GetProperty("status").GetInt32();

// safe reading(Field may not exist)
if (result.TryGetProperty("optional", out var field))
{
    string val = field.GetString()!;
}

// Traverse array
foreach (var item in result.GetProperty("nodes").EnumerateArray())
{
    Console.WriteLine(item.GetProperty("nodeId").GetString());
}
